clue.text: Sailor ditching a map that's back-to- front

indicators.note: to ditch something is to throw it away, so the named letter is dropped from the word
back-to-front describes something facing the wrong way, so the remaining letters are read in the opposite order

blocks.note: taken as written; this is the letter to be dropped
an atlas is a book of maps

explanation.surface: A sailor throws away a chart that was the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: ATLAS loses its first A to leave TLAS, which turned round gives SALT.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a seasoned seaman, so salt alone serves as a slang synonym for a sailor.

clue.text: Commanding officer charging forward and back

indicators.note: charging means loading, as a gun is charged, so one piece is loaded into the other

blocks.note: to forward a letter is to send it on
CO is the standard abbreviation for commanding officer

explanation.surface: An officer leads a charge forward, then retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charging forward and back' reads as a battlefield advance and retreat; 'charging' is the insertion signal and 'back' is a verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion is to support it formally, which is what backing a proposal means.

clue.text: Unloading, remove the last of the bolts

indicators.note: to remove is to take away, so a letter comes out of the word
the last of a word is its final letter, which picks out one letter only

blocks.note: unloading a cargo makes it lighter, so it is lightening
the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Someone unloading a crate is told to take out the last of the bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolts' looks like hardware being unloaded, but it is the definition: lightning bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightning comes in bolts, the flashes of electrical discharge from a storm cloud.

clue.text: Where chess is played fairly

blocks.note: first meaning: literally above the board, where the pieces and players' hands are
second meaning: honestly and openly, without trickery

explanation.surface: A description of a chess game conducted honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about fair play at chess; split it after 'played' and each half defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Above board is an idiom for honest and open, from card players keeping hands visible above the table.

clue.text: Protected animal attempts to eat environmentalist's face and attacks

indicators.note: the face is the front of something, so only the first letter is kept
eating takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: bats are a legally protected species in the UK
attempts are tries
the first letter of environmentalist

explanation.surface: A protected creature tries to bite a conservationist's face and attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: In British law bats are protected, which makes them a natural 'protected animal'. Batteries are a series of blows, as in assault and battery.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery is a sustained bombardment or assault, so batteries means attacks as a plural noun.

clue.text: Judgments reached by ill-treated wives

indicators.note: something ill-treated is knocked about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mistreated wives come to their own conclusions about their husbands.
explanation.definitionFit: Views are opinions, the considered judgments someone holds on a matter.

clue.text: Empty bureau, under which King Charles' housemaid's left Champagne?

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, so only the outer letters remain
'housemaid's left' means the servant has departed, so her name leaves the word

blocks.note: the first and last letters of bureau
BB King was the American blues guitarist
the name taken as written
a char, or charwoman, is a cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A cleared-out bureau beneath which a royal servant has left a bottle of fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Charles' looks like one royal, but King is the American blues guitarist BB King, and the housemaid is a char, British slang for a cleaning lady. In a down clue 'under which' places what follows lower in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubbles is informal slang for champagne or any sparkling wine; the question mark flags the casual name.

clue.text: I spent a morning in bed, which is unusual

indicators.note: something spent is used up and gone, so that letter disappears from the word

blocks.note: the letter to be removed, taken as written
taken as written
a lie-in is a morning spent lying in bed

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a lazy morning in bed, out of character for them.
explanation.walkthrough: A LIE-IN loses its second I to leave ALIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign or strange, so something alien to a person is unusual for them.

clue.text: Ugly lines made by car lover with Tesla regularly driven out

indicators.note: driving out every other letter at regular intervals keeps the alternate ones left behind

blocks.note: British slang for someone who has sex in parked cars, known as dogging
the second and fourth letters of Tesla

explanation.surface: Bad verse written by a motoring enthusiast after his Tesla was driven away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car lover' suggests a motoring fan, but it is cheeky British slang for someone who goes dogging in car parks.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is crude, badly made verse, so its poor lines are ugly ones.

clue.text: Dirty and slippery rugby ball initially held

indicators.note: something slippery slides about, so these letters slide into a new arrangement
initially points to the first letter of the word next to it
something held is clasped inside, so that letter goes within the others

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of ball

explanation.surface: A muddy, slippery rugby ball is held by a player.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubby is an everyday synonym for dirty, covered in grime.

clue.text: Rolled paper letter a GI carefully carries west

indicators.note: carries means holds inside, so the answer is held within the run of words
in an across clue going west means reading from right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of letter, a, GI and the start of carefully

explanation.surface: A soldier carefully carries a rolled-up letter westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolled paper letter' reads as one item; the definition stops at 'paper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarette is tobacco wrapped in a rolled tube of thin paper.

clue.text: Get jewels by singing, not fighting

indicators.note: not means without, so the fighting word is taken out of the singing word

blocks.note: warbling is singing with trills
war is fighting between nations

explanation.definitionFit: Bling is slang for flashy jewellery, ostentatious gems and gold worn for show.

clue.text: That which distinguishes tennis from Ping-Pong is striking

definitions.text: That which distinguishes tennis from Ping-Pong

blocks.clueFragment: That which distinguishes tennis from Ping-Pong
blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: Ping-Pong is table tennis, and ordinary tennis has none
second meaning: remarkable, worthy of attention

explanation.surface: A remark about what sets lawn tennis apart from its indoor cousin.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NO TABLE: that is the difference between tennis and table tennis. 'Striking' sounds like hitting a ball but means remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means worth noticing, which is what a striking thing is.

clue.text: Mum's spoiled nieces left bored

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined, so these letters are wrecked into a new order
to bore is to drill into, so that letter is drilled inside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A mother has indulged her nieces, who have now been left bored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother; it is the noun from 'mum's the word', meaning saying nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum as a noun or adjective means saying nothing, from the idiom keeping mum, so it equals quiet.

clue.text: Intercourse probing 'the limits of cinematography in Casablanca'?

indicators.note: limits are boundaries, so only the first and last letters are kept
a probe pushes inside something, so that piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of cinematography
it is a coy slang word for sex

explanation.surface: A film critic's question about how far the love scenes in the classic film Casablanca push the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: Casablanca looks like the film; the definition is the Moroccan city of that name, given as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Casablanca is the largest city in Morocco, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Prime policeman to escape unseen

indicators.note: the escapee gets out, so those letters leave the larger word

blocks.note: a prime number cannot be divided by any number except itself and one
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A leading police officer gets away without being seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' looks like an adjective for the policeman; it is a number that is indivisible, and DI walks out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Invisible means unable to be seen, the same sense as unseen.

clue.text: Disc inserted in new Megadrive after wrapper finally removed?

definitions.text: Disc inserted in new Megadrive after wrapper finally removed?

indicators.note: removed means taken out, so that letter leaves the word
finally points to the last letter of the word before it
new suggests a fresh version, so the letters are remade into a different order
inserted in means placed inside, so that letter goes into the middle

blocks.note: taken as written; the Mega Drive was a Sega games console
the last letter of wrapper
a disc is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Unwrapping a new Sega console and putting a disc in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mega Drive was Sega's 1990s games console. Read whole, the clue also describes what you do to start a computer game, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a disc into a freshly unwrapped games console is how you start playing a computer game.

clue.text: The end of Star Trek?

blocks.note: surface reading: the final episode of the science-fiction television series
setter's reading: the wise men's journey following the Nativity star, which ended at the town of Jesus's birth

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest the TV franchise; read lower-case, it is the journey of the Magi following the star in the Gospel of Matthew.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi followed the star until it stopped over the town of Jesus's birth, the end of their trek.

clue.text: Really loud soldiers shoot indiscriminately

indicators.note: firing indiscriminately is firing at random, so these letters land in random order

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Noisy troops fire wildly in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Really loud' looks like one phrase; 'Really' is the definition and 'loud' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsooth is an archaic exclamation meaning in truth, used like indeed or truly.

clue.text: Tight orange Sainsbury's top I'd put on

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Sainsbury's
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight orange top' looks like clothing; 'Tight' means drunk and the definition is 'put on', as an event is put on.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on an event is to stage or arrange it, so a staged event has been organised.

clue.text: Book groups

blocks.note: first meaning: the fourth book of the Old Testament
second meaning: bodies of people

explanation.definitionFit: Numbers is the Bible book recording the census of Israel, and numbers also means groups or quantities of people.

clue.text: Bright front of cabaret bar

blocks.note: the first letter of cabaret

clue.text: Piece of fruit aristocrat very gently inserted

clue.text: Different ways ladies promote love for flaky white guys
